summary: Scoped administration (E3.3): activate administration as ordinary delegable grants on the reserved mgmt_object:* resource-type (no separate admin subsystem) and ship the day-1 admin-narrowing checker — a pure, IO-free function (validateAdminDelegation, likely src/core/scoped-admin.ts) that proves a delegated mgmt-grant or role-assignment is a structural subset of the granting admin's own authority along BOTH axes (resource/org scope via T-0018 validateNarrowing; org/admin boundary via the T-0022 role_assignment.org_scope, using the existing isNarrowerOrEqual/AncestryOracle — no new scope algebra). The single genesis tenant-owner (already seeded by T-0022, currently grant-less) is the un-parented delegation root via an INJECTED isGenesisOwner boolean (per T-0018 ADR). T-0029 adds idempotent dev-silo seeds (migrations numbered >=026; 022=T-0034, 023-025=T-0062 in flight) that wire the tenant-owner role to delegable mgmt_object:role|agent|process|grant grants rooted at the tenant-root org node + a confirmed genesis assignment, making the owner a real fully-capable mgmt-admin. Self-elevation is rejected as a corollary of narrowing (adversarial fitness proof). HTTP write-routes / grant-editor UI are T-0030 (E3.4) — day-1 = pure checker + contract + seed, no HTTP route needed for AC verifiability. grant-resolver.ts is NOT edited (admin narrowing is write-path; read-path PDP untouched). No new tenant table is required day-1 (mgmt-grant seeds ride the existing grant table); FR-7/AC-16 cover the new-table branch additively (known_tenant_tables.txt + cross_tenant seedRowForTable case, the T-0062 lesson). 17 CI-checkable acceptance criteria. No blocking questions (GT-1 signed).
functional: FR-1 mgmt_object:* is a first-class lattice-resident resource-type family: management objects (role, agent registry, processes, the rights/grants themselves) are administered via ORDINARY grant rows with resource_type in {mgmt_object:role, mgmt_object:agent, mgmt_object:process, mgmt_object:grant}; no separate admin table/flag/role-kind; mgmt-grant scope is an org-hierarchy ScopeElement (hierarchy:org, nodeLevel department|position); operation from the existing Operation union (create/read/update/delete, plus invoke for mgmt_object:agent).

FR-2 monotonic narrowing on the admin write-path (core deliverable): a pure function rejects-before-persistence any delegated grant/assignment that is not a structural subset of the granting admin's authority along BOTH axes — (1) resource/org-scope axis via T-0018 validateNarrowing(adminGrant, child, oracle) with adminGrant.delegable===true and non-widening facet/constraint; (2) org/admin-scope axis: the target's org context must be subset-or-equal of the admin's administering assignment org_scope SET, via existing isNarrowerOrEqual/AncestryOracle. Distinct typed rejection (extends T-0018 NarrowingResult, e.g. org_scope_widens); never mutates/persists/does IO.

FR-3 no self-elevation (provable security invariant): no admin can grant authority they do not hold; this is a COROLLARY of FR-2 (a self-elevating child is not subset of the granter, so validateNarrowing rejects it), proven by an adversarial fitness test over mgmt_object:* node/tag/interval/set/org-subtree fuzz (mirrors grant-lattice.adversarial.test.ts) — a child widening any axis is ALWAYS rejected.

FR-4 genesis tenant-owner is the un-parented delegation root: exactly one tenant-owner per tenant; owner-minted grants are NOT subset-checked against a parent (none exists above the owner); 'is this principal the genesis owner?' is an INJECTED boolean (T-0018 ADR genesis-owner identity), not a lattice concern; every grant the owner delegates downward becomes a subset-checked parent; the owner is the only principal that may mint a freeform mgmt-grant (forced delegable=false, reuses T-0018 FR-6).

FR-5 genesis bootstrap chain (seed): additive idempotent dev-silo seeds make the seeded tenant-owner a real fully-capable mgmt-admin — (1) delegable mgmt-grants {mgmt_object:role|agent|process|grant, create|read|update|delete, scope=tenant-root org node} on the tenant-owner role; (2) a confirmed genesis assignment wiring a genesis owner employee (human) to tenant-owner with org_scope=tenant-root node. Stable UUIDs + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; migration file(s) numbered from 026; FK-ordered (role->grant; employee->role_assignment); re-run = identical counts.

FR-6 delegated administration bounded to the assignment subtree(s): a non-owner admin (e.g. HR admin with mgmt_object:role within the hr subtree) may create/edit roles/assignments ONLY within their administering assignment's org_scope ceiling — applies FR-2's org-axis; AC matrix includes a within-subtree (accepted) and an escaping-subtree (rejected) case.

FR-7 mgmt_object known to the tenant-table/cross-tenant harness: if T-0029 adds a NEW tenant table it is appended additively to ci/checks/known_tenant_tables.txt and given its own seedRowForTable case (per-tenant seed row) in cross_tenant.test.ts (the T-0062 lesson); if it adds NO new table (default — mgmt-grant seeds ride the existing grant table) this FR is satisfied vacuously and the contract states so.

FR-8 removing the role removes the capability (not just hides UI): admin capability is ONLY the mgmt-grants reachable through confirmed in-window assignments (T-0021/T-0022 resolution contract); revoking the assignment / expiring its window / deleting the mgmt-grant removes the capability at the authority layer; day-1 proof = a subject with no confirmed in-window mgmt_object:* grant fails validateAdminDelegation for every delegation.
non_functional: NF-1 no second authority subsystem: admin authority expressed solely as grant rows (mgmt_object:* x operation x org-scope); static fitness lint asserts no admin-specific table/flag/role-kind/ACL store (mirrors T-0018 AC-11).
NF-2 no new scope algebra: both narrowing axes reuse grant-lattice.ts (validateNarrowing, isNarrowerOrEqual, AncestryOracle); no new ScopeElement kind, no parallel containment path.
NF-3 pure IO-free checker: validateAdminDelegation does no DB/network/LLM IO (ancestry injected via oracle); equal inputs => equal output; the DB write-path that calls it is T-0030.

NF-4 read-path core untouched: grant-resolver.ts is NOT edited (admin narrowing is write-path); a new pure module (e.g. src/core/scoped-admin.ts) may IMPORT grant-lattice.ts but must not change its exported signatures (additive-only if touched at all).
NF-5 T-0013 tenant invariants on any DDL: FORCE RLS, default-DENY, tenant_id leading, choros_app grant; additive migration numbering from 026; idempotent seeds.
NF-6 genesis owner unique per tenant: seed + fitness check assert exactly one tenant-owner role per tenant (the lattice root is unambiguous).

NF-7 forward-compat frozen surfaces: the mgmt_object:* day-1 kind set, the genesis-owner injected-flag contract, and the checker's typed-rejection union are frozen for the sibling consumers T-0030 (write-API/UI) and T-0039 (LLM-proposes).
out_of_scope: HTTP write-routes / structural-grant editor UI for minting mgmt-grants and assignments = T-0030 (E3.4); T-0029 ships the pure narrowing checker + its contract, T-0030 is the write-API that calls it before INSERT (day-1 ACs are provable without an HTTP route via pure checker + adversarial fitness + live seed probe).
LLM-proposes-grants / human-confirms = T-0039 (E3.5); T-0029 only fixes that no grant is effective without confirmed_by (T-0022 contract).
DB-backed getGrants resolution (role_assignment->grant JOIN under RLS) = T-0053; the confirmed+in-window+org_scope-admits CONTRACT is reused from T-0022, the live query is T-0053.
Read-path PDP enforcement for mgmt_object handles; grant-resolver.ts is NOT edited (admin narrowing is a write-path invariant).
Agent provisioning / 'hiring' runtime mechanics + Keycloak service-account = T-0043/E5.1+; T-0029 only reserves mgmt_object:agent + invoke as the grant shape.
role_criticality / dual-control on mgmt writes = T-0040/T-0044 (E4.5/E4.6); D-A=A3 dual-control is a separate gate layered on top, T-0029 supplies the grant rows it reads.
multi-tenant pooled provisioning (silo N=1 dev seed only).

acceptance_criteria.text: mgmt_object:* is a first-class resource-type: a grant fixture with resource_type in {mgmt_object:role, mgmt_object:agent, mgmt_object:process, mgmt_object:grant} is a structurally valid Grant (compile-checked against the T-0018 ResourceType union); a static lint asserts these are the day-1 mgmt-object kinds.

The admin-narrowing checker ACCEPTS a delegated mgmt-grant whose scope is subset-or-equal of adminGrant.scope (org subtree of the admin's), with adminGrant.delegable===true and non-widening facet/constraint — returns {ok:true}.

The checker REJECTS before persistence (never mutates) a delegated mgmt-grant whose org-scope WIDENS the admin's (child is ancestor/sibling-subtree, or escapes the admin's org_scope set) — distinct typed rejection (scope_widens / org_scope_widens).

No self-elevation (adversarial): for fuzz-generated mgmt_object:* parent/child pairs across node/tag/interval/set/org-subtree, a child widening ANY axis is ALWAYS rejected; only genuine subsets are accepted (mirrors grant-lattice.adversarial.test.ts).

Non-delegable / freeform parent rejected: admin grant delegable=false => parent_non_delegable; admin grant scope freeform => free_form_non_delegable; a non-owner minting a freeform mgmt-grant is rejected.

Genesis owner is the un-parented root: with injected isGenesisOwner=true an owner-minted mgmt-grant is accepted WITHOUT a parent-subset check (no parent required); with isGenesisOwner=false and no covering admin grant the same write is rejected (no_admin_authority / no_grant).

Delegated admin bounded to subtree: an admin assigned mgmt_object:role within subtree S is accepted for a role/assignment whose org context is subset-or-equal of S, and rejected for one outside S — using the existing org AncestryOracle.

No second authority subsystem: a static fitness lint asserts admin authority is expressed only as grant rows on mgmt_object:* — no admin-specific table/flag/role-kind/ACL store exists in the model fixture (mirrors T-0018 AC-11).

No new scope algebra: a static check asserts the admin checker imports isNarrowerOrEqual/validateNarrowing/AncestryOracle from grant-lattice.ts and defines no new ScopeElement kind and no parallel containment function.
Checker is pure (IO-free): a static lint asserts the admin-checker module performs no DB/network/LLM IO and accepts an injected oracle; equal inputs => equal output (property test).
grant-resolver.ts unchanged: a static check asserts src/core/grant-resolver.ts is byte-for-byte unedited by this task (read-path untouched; admin narrowing is write-path).

Genesis seed present + idempotent: after migrate (and a double-run) exactly the seeded mgmt-grants are attached to tenant-owner and exactly one confirmed genesis assignment wires the genesis owner employee -> tenant-owner at the tenant-root org node; re-run yields identical counts (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING).
Exactly one genesis owner per tenant: a fitness/seed check asserts the tenant-owner role is unique per tenant and the genesis assignment is the single un-parented root.

Removing the role removes the capability: a resolver-contract/checker fixture shows a subject whose tenant-owner (or delegated-admin) assignment is revoked or out-of-window confers ZERO mgmt authority — validateAdminDelegation rejects every delegation for them (capability gone at the authority layer, not UI).

Audit obligation on mgmt-grant issuance/revocation: every mgmt-grant create/revoke call site is accompanied by a GrantAuditEvent emit carrying actor, subject (role_id), capability (resource_type x operation x facet), scope, and (when present) proposed_by/confirmed_by (reuses T-0018 FR-7; static lint on call sites).

Tenant-table / cross-tenant harness coherence: if T-0029 adds a new tenant table it appears in known_tenant_tables.txt and has a seedRowForTable case with a per-tenant seed row (cross-tenant probe green); if it adds none, a check confirms the mgmt-grant seeds ride the already-registered grant table and no known_tenant_tables.txt change is needed.

Migration numbering seam: any migration T-0029 ships is numbered >= 026 (022/023-025 reserved by T-0034/T-0062 in flight), is additive (no edit to prior migrations), and keeps T-0013 invariants (FORCE RLS / default-DENY / tenant_id leading) on any DDL.
